location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md:32 (Never: headless config copy) vs :24 (Configured cells, aggregate --config)
issue: Headless config copy is deferred, but configured cells now come only from --config. The spec does not say what headless callers (psm-develop, psm-cross-version, psm-scaffold, psm-optimize) pass in this slice when they narrow versions or browsers.
implementation_impact: A headless call for one version gets ready=false from cells it never asked for. An aggregate call that still passes the caller's --versions hits the new exit 2 for a --versions that differs from config. Either way the per-version verdict contract of the headless callers breaks.
suggestion: State the interim headless rule. Either pull the config-copy step into this slice, or say that headless keeps its current behavior and never passes --versions to the aggregate, and spell out which configured set applies.

location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md:32 (Never: e2e_step/e2e_next_cells/run scope) and :69 (docs: Fase 1/2 e2e commands)
issue: e2e_step and e2e_next_cells are deferred, yet the docs task rewrites the Fase 1/2 E2E commands. The spec never says how the orchestrator turns the new per-cell rerun_matrix entries into a --cells or --versions argument.
implementation_impact: SKILL.md and run-phases.md will say something the scripts do not decide. The orchestrator may pick cells by judgment, rerun browsers that already pass, or pass an argument the new rules reject (--per-version).
suggestion: Give the interim rule. For example: group the layer-e2e rerun_matrix entries by version into --cells <ver>:<b>[+<b>] (one invocation, default --jobs), and use no other source of cells.

location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md:26 (layer e2e input errors) vs cell-contract.md Runner > Input errors
issue: Only some of the contract's Runner input errors are named for this slice (one of --cells/--versions, and --per-version). The status of the others is left open: --tier missing or invalid, --jobs, --warm, --scenarios-from-failed, a repeated version in --cells, a cell outside the configured set, --cells with another layer.
implementation_impact: One implementer may add a required --tier because the contract says so, which breaks every documented command. Another may accept repeated versions or cells outside the configured set, which writes histories that no reader looks at.
suggestion: List every Runner input error explicitly, each with in-slice or deferred: --tier absent and rejected by argparse; --jobs accepted; repeated version, outside-config cell and --cells with another layer are exit 2.

issue: The contract's TDD verdict command includes --tier 0, but --tier is deferred. The spec does not say which form the quickstart doc should use.
implementation_impact: A doc copied from the contract tells users to run a command that exits 2 on an unknown flag.
suggestion: Say that the quickstart step in this slice is `ps-run-layer.py --layer e2e --cells … --session <token>` with no --tier, followed by `ps-aggregate.py --reports-dir`.

issue: ps-run-layer is stopped with --stop-job while children run. stopped records are deferred, and the spec does not say what ps-run-layer appends for the admitted cells.
implementation_impact: The children exit 143 with no output, so the generic no-result path appends crash records. A crash record is an infra cause, so an operator stop later counts toward blocked-infra. The other option, appending nothing, is also unstated.
suggestion: State the rule: when the run is stopped (JobStopped or SIGTERM), append no record for cells without a child result, and do not apply the crash rule to children killed by that stop.

issue: Some version-level failures happen before any engine is driven: skipped_image, compose unavailable, bring-up error, port-conflict retry, not healthy, install failure, no HTTP. The spec does not say whether the child still emits cells for every requested engine in these cases.
implementation_impact: When cells is empty, ps-run-layer finds no per-cell result and writes crash. The real reason (errors or install) is lost, and the copy of errors and install into each cell, which the contract requires, never happens.
suggestion: Require the child to emit `cells[engine] = {driven: false, launch_error: null, ...}` for every engine in --engines on every return path after the probe. Reserve crash for children that produce no parseable output.

issue: The child output may name a version not requested, carry cells for an engine that was not admitted, lack a cell for an admitted engine, or fail validate_layer_shape. Today these cases cause exit 2 (rejected) or a missing-version result. History mode has no rule for them.
implementation_impact: Stray records could be appended to the wrong cell's history, or an admitted cell could silently get no record. The exit code would be unpredictable.
suggestion: Write the rule: ignore and log any cell outside the admitted set; give an admitted engine with no cell a crash record; treat output that fails the shape gate as no output, so the crash rule applies.

issue: One child exits 2 while other version children are queued or running under --jobs. not-run production is deferred, and the spec does not say whether the others start or whether their records are appended.
implementation_impact: Following today's code (return 2 before writing) drops valid records from the children that finished. Following the contract would need not-run records, which this slice cannot produce.
suggestion: State the rule: queued children still run; every other child's records are appended; the exit-2 version gets no record; ps-run-layer exits 2 after appending.

issue: ps-run-layer --layer e2e --versions 9.2 (not configured) or --versions 9.1.0 when 9.1 is configured. Exact-string matching is required only for canary and --cells versions.
implementation_impact: A history named with a non-configured string (for example -9.1.0-) is never read, so the run looks successful but is invisible to plan and aggregate. Plan --per-version --versions 9.2 would also emit browser-keyed e2e for a version that is not configured.
suggestion: Extend the exact configured-string match to ps-run-layer --versions for e2e (exit 2), and say how plan and aggregate treat a --versions entry outside the configured set.

issue: --config is given, but psm_target_versions or psm_e2e_browsers is absent, null or an empty string. The spec does not say whether this means the script defaults or an empty list (exit 2). Reading or parsing the --config file can also fail.
implementation_impact: Plan, runner and aggregate may resolve different configured sets from the same file, so cells planned as required do not match the cells the aggregate gates on.
suggestion: State in the normalizer: key absent or null means the script default; a present empty string means exit 2; an unreadable or non-object config means exit 2. Use this one function in all three scripts.

location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md:24 (State/freshness incl. reports-dir exclusion) vs Runner input errors
issue: The fingerprint rule depends on rejecting psm_reports_dir equal to the module root, and a passthrough --screenshot-dir inside the module but outside the reports dir. The spec does not list these Runner input errors, or the equivalent checks in plan and aggregate, as in scope.
implementation_impact: Screenshots written inside the module change the fingerprint during every run, so every new record is stale the moment it is written. A reports dir at the module root makes the exclusion ambiguous.
suggestion: Name both checks as in-slice exit 2 in ps-run-layer, plus the reports-dir check in plan and aggregate, wherever source_fingerprint is computed.

issue: Appending to a history fails: OSError, disk full, flock error, or a reports dir that is missing or read-only.
implementation_impact: The exit code is unspecified. Some cells may be recorded and others not, and the output line's `appended` list may claim records that were never written.
suggestion: Write the rule: on append failure, log the path, leave it out of `appended`, keep appending the other cells, and exit 2 (or the stated code) after all cells are tried.

issue: In --merge-only --layer e2e, the view value for a configured cell with no history, or with corrupt-history, is not stated. Nor is what happens when --versions or --session is also passed.
implementation_impact: The view's shape is inconsistent (missing key vs null vs a placeholder). If --versions is still required by argparse, the contract's form of the command (no --versions) cannot run.
suggestion: Define it: a cell with no valid record gets `cells[ver][b] = null`; --versions and --session are rejected with exit 2, or ignored (choose one); --versions is not required for layer e2e.

issue: The aggregate is called with explicit --static and no --reports-dir or --module, which the CLI still allows.
implementation_impact: There is no history location, so every cell reads as missing with no error, or the code fails on a None path.
suggestion: Make --reports-dir and --module required whenever the E2E layer is evaluated, or exit 2 when e2e is in --require and they are absent.

location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md:24 (aggregate per-version e2e_state/reason, reason as in plan)
issue: A version has cells with different reasons, for example chromium missing and firefox stale-source. Plan reasons such as not-gradeable and scenario-notes also need the current e2e_scenario_notes, and the spec does not say whether the aggregate computes them.
implementation_impact: The aggregate may report a different reason than the plan for the same cell, or pick an arbitrary cell's reason for versions[ver].reason.
suggestion: State that versions[ver].reason is the reason of the first cell without passing evidence, in psm_e2e_browsers order. State that the aggregate computes current e2e_scenario_notes through the same discover_scenarios loader the plan uses.

issue: The last line of a history is corrupt and an earlier valid line is a passing gate-grade record. Aggregate selection still picks that pass.
implementation_impact: e2e_cells shows state pass with gate_grade true next to reason corrupt-history. Consumers reading `state` may treat the cell as proven.
suggestion: Say that when corrupt-history applies, e2e_cells[ver][b] gets gate_grade false and state inconclusive, with reason corrupt-history, whatever the selected record says.

issue: The timing sink has gaps. A direct ps-e2e-run.py run with several --versions holds several versions in one process. A phase can exit by exception (JobStopped, timeout). And the outcome values are not listed.
implementation_impact: Phases from one version leak into the next one's boot_phases as #2 entries. The outcome strings may not match between producers and tests.
suggestion: Reset the sink per run_one_version call. Enumerate outcome as ok, the phase status string, or error on exception, and record the entry in __exit__ whatever the outcome. Make the sink a no-op when inactive (Layer 2/5 phases).

issue: The child's emitted image_tag differs from the tag ps-run-layer resolved from its passthrough and config tag map.
implementation_impact: The spec does not say which value the merged record stores. Freshness may then compare against a tag that was not actually booted, or reject valid evidence.
suggestion: Write the rule: the child's image_tag wins in the merge; a mismatch with ps-run-layer's resolved tag is logged, and the record keeps the child value so it reads stale-tag.

issue: The config sets psm_e2e_canary outside the configured cells, or malformed. The canary is deferred, but the normalizer text mentions canary matching.
implementation_impact: Some scripts in this slice may exit 2 on the canary and others may ignore it, so the same config is valid for plan but rejected by the aggregate, or the other way round.
suggestion: State whether psm_e2e_canary is validated in this slice. Recommended: ignored by all three scripts until CAP-1.
